title: Measurement: setup asks before it looks, binds a model only on an explicit confirmation, and settles the research decision separately
summary: TSK-0060 SLICE 3, toward ACC-0054 and — not yet evaluated — ACC-0106, ACC-0107, ACC-0043, ACC-0045, ACC-0085 and ACC-0108. The implementation is commit 4313e6e with its fixture correction in 5aaa2da; the sha256 of each file is in the facts. THE ORDER, AND WHAT IT PROTECTS. After the package is registered, setup obtains permission to inspect this computer's connections, and only then discovers models, binds one, proves its credential contract and settles the separate web-research decision. Pi's authentication store, its custom-model registry and the presence of any credential variable are all behind that one answer. Each phase is declared, and each is the existing writer's work rather than a second copy of it: `inspectWithConsent` for the grant and the discovery, `selectModel` for the choice, the confirmation, the grant and the settings write, `resolveProviderCredentials` for the contract, and `setUpResearch` for the Tavily decision. WHAT THE COMMAND ADDS. `--provider` and `--model` are given together or not at all; `--thinking` and `--research tavily|disabled` are their own. One typed line is turned into what these modules expect: an explicit yes or no becomes a boolean, a list choice stays a line, and a closed input is null — so an answer the command cannot read is never recorded as a decision, in any phase. A run with nobody to ask does not ask: it answers null without prompting, which records nothing, and hands the selection no `ask` at all, so a model nobody confirmed cannot be committed. A partial run — an inspection nobody allowed, a model nobody confirmed, a cancelled choice — exits 9 with the project, its identity, its protected runtime directory and its registered package all valid and the reason printed. NOTHING OF THIS HOST IS TOUCHED BEFORE THE ANSWER, AND IT IS OBSERVED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. A child runs the real command with Node's own fs, environment and network boundaries recorded from before it starts, and every question is recorded with the counts as they stood when it was asked. At the inspection question, and across a whole declined run: zero reads of any auth.json or models.json, ZERO ENVIRONMENT EVENTS OF ANY KIND — with OPENAI_API_KEY set in that environment — and no network. THE TRUST DECISION IS TAKEN IN A CHILD, AND THAT IS WHY THE COUNT IS ZERO (corrected in 3317fff). Loading Pi's SDK enumerates the environment: its bundled `debug` calls Object.keys(process.env) at module load to find its own settings, which was traced to debug/src/node.js inside the Pi bundle rather than inferred. It reads no value, but an enumeration shows which credential variables this computer has, and presence is exactly what this consent gates. The trust store is Pi's and the proposal orders trust before the inspection, so this process cannot both take that decision and stay out of the environment. Masking `process.env` in place does not fix it and was rejected on measurement: hiding a name through a proxy makes the engine verify the omission against the target, which touches the very names being hidden, and building a filtered copy means first seeing which of them exist. So `lib/pi-trust-child.mjs` takes the decision in a child started with an environment built by NAMING variables — the list CMP-0029 measured for a child that holds no credential, plus Pi's own locators when the operator set them — and this process loads no Pi until the operator has allowed it. A host with every credential variable of every supported provider set, plus the research credential, hands that child none of them and nothing the list does not name. AND THE CHILD'S REPORT IS CHECKED BEFORE IT IS A DECISION. A parseable JSON line is not one: the report crosses a process boundary and everything after it acts on the answer, so the state must be one Pi's store can give, the action asked for must be the state that came back, the project must be the one this run is setting up, and the agent directory must be named. An approval for another project, an approval answering a denial, an unknown state, a missing project or agent directory, and a non-object are each refused. A child that exits non-zero may have written the decision and failed on the read-back that proves it landed, so the refusal says the result could not be verified rather than promising nothing changed. RESULTS, THROUGH THE REAL COMMAND. (1) A complete run commits provider, model and thinking level to .pi/settings.json and records this host's model-use grant in the ignored runtime directory; neither file contains the stored key's sentinel. (2) A declined inspection stops the phases that depend on it, records the decline, and still settles the research choice, which "not-inspected" is a state that writer records without looking at anything. (3) A closed input records nothing at all — no consent file is written. (4) A changed selection moves both the committed model and the grant; a declined change leaves both exactly as they were. (5) A rerun that names nothing asks nothing and rewrites nothing: the committed selection and its approval are read back and reused, byte-identically. (6) With no Tavily credential the operator is not asked and no grant is recorded; with one present the question is asked and a no records the project's choice with the connection never checked. (7) A non-interactive run asks nothing, records nothing and commits no model. (8) A provider with no credential contract — the fixture's loopback custom provider — is refused by name. THE FIXTURES ARE THE REAL LAYOUT, AND NOTHING BILLABLE IS REACHABLE. Each project is a Git repository whose `.planning` is this checkout, with its own Pi agent directory holding a stored sentinel key for OpenAI and a custom provider pointed at a closed loopback port. Discovery is Pi's own registry, built with its network disabled; no inference is performed anywhere in these slices, and no case answers yes to the research question, because a yes is what makes the probe contact Tavily. A TEST THAT MEASURED THE MACHINE, FOUND BY CI. The first push passed locally and failed in all four cells: this computer has a real TAVILY_API_KEY in its environment, so setup found a connection and asked, while CI has none and did not. The presence of that variable decides whether the question is asked at all, so the harness now owns it — absent unless a case asks for it, and then an obvious fake — and the two paths are separate cases. Recorded here because the defect was in the measurement, not in the command. LIMITS. R9 is still half closed, and it is the remaining TSK-0060 work that owes it. The registration refusals no longer print as stack traces — this slice's failure reporting prints any of Kiln's refusal classes as the written refusal it carries — but they all share the generic setup exit code, and which code each class deserves is the mapping that task still owes. Setup supplies no custom credential declaration, so a custom provider cannot be bound (D25, D13). `--local-state user` refuses by name. The preflight canary, the live model check, the read-back and the full exit-code mapping are slice 4, and the spanning criteria stay not-evaluated until the integration record. No model request is made by any phase in this slice, so nothing here proves the selected model works — that is what slice 4's live check is for. MUTATIONS, RUN LOCALLY ON WINDOWS. Nineteen changes across three sets, each restored byte-identical by sha256. Eighteen were caught: the inspection run without consent, a declined inspection still choosing a model, an unreadable answer counted as a yes, a run with nobody to ask asking anyway, a partial setup reported as complete, the credential contract not proved, the research decision skipped, Pi loaded in this process before consent (twice, against two different controls), the child inheriting this process's environment, the child environment builder copying whatever it is given, a failed trust child treated as a decision, any parseable line accepted as a decision, a report about another project accepted, the state unchecked, an approval answering a denial, an unnamed agent directory accepted, and a failed child promising nothing changed. THE ONE THAT SURVIVES is dropping the derived skill-override entry from the selection's settings write, which no supported layout can distinguish while every non-default content root is refused — the same blind spot R9 leaves in slice 2.

facts.implementation: commits 4313e6e (slice 3), 5aaa2da (the fixture correction), 3317fff (the trust child, which is what makes the consent boundary hold) and 5633ec3 (the report validation)
facts.tests: test/setup-command.test.mjs: 26 tests, 20 of which run the real main(); one of those runs it in a child with every access recorded. The rest hold exported functions directly, the import graph being a static scan.
facts.phases: inspection, model, credential-contract and research, each declared, after trust and registration
facts.order-observed: at the inspection question and across a whole declined run: 0 environment events of any kind, 0 reads of any auth.json or models.json with OPENAI_API_KEY set, and 0 network
facts.environment-before-consent: none. The trust decision runs in lib/pi-trust-child.mjs, a child whose environment is built by naming variables, so this process loads no Pi — and therefore touches no environment — before the operator has allowed it
facts.complete-run: provider, model and thinking level committed to .pi/settings.json; the model-use grant recorded in the ignored runtime directory; neither file contains the fixture's stored-key sentinel
facts.declined-inspection: exit 9, the decline recorded, the research choice still settled as not-inspected, the project valid
facts.closed-input: exit 9 with no consent file written at all
facts.changed-selection: the committed model and the grant both move; a declined change leaves both as they were
facts.rerun: a rerun that names nothing asks nothing and changes no bytes
facts.research: with no credential the operator is not asked and no grant is recorded; with one present the question is asked and a no records the project's choice with the connection never checked
facts.non-interactive: asks nothing, records nothing, commits no model, exit 9
facts.custom-provider: refused by name for want of a credential contract (D25)
facts.no-billable-provider: Pi's registry is built with its network disabled, the fixture's custom provider points at a closed loopback port, no inference is performed, and no case answers yes to the research question
facts.mutations: 19 run locally on Windows across three sets, 18 killed, 1 survives (the derived skill entry, unobservable while every non-default content root is refused); each restored byte-identical by sha256

omissions.reason: No phase in this slice makes a model request, so nothing here shows the selected model works. That is slice 4's preflight canary and live check.
No case answers yes to the research question, because the probe is what contacts Tavily. What a probe does is measured in the research component's own tests against an injected fetch.
Setup supplies no custom credential declaration, so a custom provider is refused rather than bound (D25, D13).
R9 remains half closed: the skill entry is derived and proved, but every content root other than <project>/planning-content is refused, which is also why the surviving mutation is unobservable.
